name: tabular_kaggle_leaky
title: The defective twin: target-derived features, encoding and imputation before the split, SMOTE on the test half, early stopping on the test set
origin: hardening round 1, tester domain-tabular: the defective half of the Kaggle-style pair

expected.defect: the ordinal encoder is fitted on the whole frame eleven lines before the split
expected.why: the category codes, and the 'unknown' bucket that goes with them, are assigned with the held-out rows in view, so no test category is ever unseen

expected.defect: the median imputer is fitted on the whole feature matrix before the split
expected.why: every imputed cell in the training half is filled from a median that the held-out rows helped compute

expected.defect: the scaler is fitted on the whole feature matrix before the split
expected.why: held-out means and variances are inside the training features

expected.defect: the scaler that was already fitted on everything is re-fitted on the held-out half and used to transform it
expected.why: the model is scored on features standardised by their own statistics rather than by the training statistics it learned from

expected.defect: cross_val_score is handed a bare LGBMClassifier over `features`, which prepare() had already imputed and scaled outside any fold
expected.why: no fold ever refits the imputer or the scaler, so the cross-validated AUC is optimistic by the same amount for every fold
the AUC printed is not reproducible, and neither is the SMOTE interpolation that follows it

expected.defect: nothing seeds numpy, the booster carries no random_state and SMOTE draws its neighbours at random
expected.why: two consecutive runs of this script disagree about which model won

unsupported.shape: a feature that is a group mean of the label column
unsupported.wouldBe: MLV105-family (target column reachable from the feature matrix); the catalogued MLV105 sketch covers `y = df['label']` left inside X, not a statistic derived from it
unsupported.why: each row's own outcome contributes to its own feature value, so validation accuracy is a memory test

unsupported.shape: SMOTE applied to the held-out half
unsupported.wouldBe: MLV104, catalogued in ISSUE_RULES section 4 and not implemented
unsupported.why: the test set becomes half synthetic rows interpolated between its own neighbours, so the metric describes an interpolation problem

unsupported.shape: early stopping on the test set
unsupported.wouldBe: MLV107, catalogued in ISSUE_RULES section 4 and not implemented
unsupported.why: the number of trees is chosen by the data the final number is reported on, so the holdout has been used for model selection

forbidden.why: the only metric is roc_auc_score, which is in the score-metric carve-out and legitimately takes continuous scores
roc_auc_score is given booster.predict_proba(test_x)[:, 1], a score column and not a hard label
there is no timestamp in this project at all - no parse_dates, no to_datetime, no date-named sort
there is no torch here and no hand-written gradient step to zero
model.eval() is a torch idiom with no LightGBM equivalent
no device is ever named in this project
prep.py fits nothing: every helper in it is a pandas expression over one frame
